_scope: Anything that touches Brazil is relevant: origin (Brazilian families or a Brazilian operator) OR target (pt-BR lure, BRA geofence, .br infrastructure, Brazilian banks). A Remcos geofenced to Brazil is in; a Mispadu that also targets Brazil is in.
_comment_target: The country being tracked. country is ISO alpha-2, geo_tags are the URLhaus geofence tags (ISO alpha-3). The accent regex flags 'ã' and 'õ', which exist in Portuguese but not in Spanish, Italian or French; the exclude regex cancels it for Vietnamese, which also uses them.
_comment_dormant: A family with no sample for more than dormant_after_days (or never recognized) is queried only every dormant_check_every_days. recent_detections still covers all of them every day.
_comment_quota: Watched RAT with no signal in the name: only the N most recent per day are queried (control sample). In the first week, ~300 queries in this group brought no signal at all.
_comment_lures: Strong lures only exist in Brazil: on their own they already send the sample to triage, because the scope is any mention of Brazil.
_comment_language: Portuguese (Brazil or Portugal), not Spanish: on their own they send the sample to 'maybe', for you to review.
_comment_weak: Portuguese or Spanish: on their own they also go to 'maybe' (threshold 20), unless the name carries a mark of another language.
_comment_hint: Generic worldwide: they only help when added to another signal.
_comment_other: Spanish or Italian marks: they remove points from an ambiguous lure. Only words that do NOT exist in Portuguese: no abbreviations ('justi' could be justificativa) and no words Portuguese also uses ('pago', 'abono'). They do not count against a strong Brazilian lure.
